subject: DPA amendment: runtime telemetry + usage carveouts — product/security review needed
messages:
From: Legal Team <legal@everreach.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@everreach.ai
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Requested DPA edits re: runtime telemetry and downstream use

Hi Priya,

Thanks for the call earlier — attaching our proposed DPA redline (EverReach_DPA_redline_v3.docx). Two items are blocking procurement on our side and we wanted to surface them explicitly so you can route to product/security:

1) Runtime telemetry carveout: we need to ensure that runtime traces that contain request/response snippets are only retained for up to 30 days and may not be used to train derivative models or analytics that infer customer PII. The current language in section 4.2 is broader than we're comfortable with.

2) Customer-origin data reuse: we're asking for an explicit carveout that prohibits using customer inputs for any model improvement unless we opt in via a separate Addendum. The redline adds a sentence in 3.1.b.

We also attached a small telemetry_sample_traces.jsonl (redacted) to show formats. Procurement wants a short confirmation by Wednesday that these two points either can be accepted or Redwood can propose compensating controls (e.g., ephemeral-only KV cache + per-tenant retention enforcement + audit logs).

If you'd prefer, we can do a 20-min call with product/security to walk through examples.

Thanks,
Claire Nguyen
Senior Counsel, EverReach Technologies

Thanks Priya — quick initial read and technical note from Security:

1) Retention: We can support a 30-day retention for telemetry snapshots if the infra team implements per-tenant lifecycle policies on the trace store and KV cache. That is operationally feasible but requires a configuration flag surfaced in the control plane (estimate: 3 sprint tickets, can be pushed as a near-term priority).

2) No-training carveout: We cannot technically prevent a model engineering team from copying redacted request/response pairs if data flows into a central training bucket; however, we can implement strict guards: per-tenant opt-out flag that stops replication to training pipelines, plus immutable audit logs of export attempts and HSM-backed markers for exported artifacts. Security recommends the following compensating controls if we cannot accept an absolute prohibition:
  - Per-tenant opt-out (control-plane flag) that prevents any routing of runtime traces to training systems.
  - Dedicated ephemeral KV namespaces for requests that auto-expire on read or at TTL boundary.
  - Audit trail + weekly attestations to customer (signed hash/timestamp) confirming no exports for opted-out tenants.

If Product can scope the control-plane flag quickly and Infra can prioritize tenant-level lifecycle enforcement, we can offer a contractual commitment to the opt-out controls with quarterly attestations. That should be acceptable to legal in many cases.

I recommend we propose that to EverReach as a compromise unless Product objects.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Director, Product Security

Thanks all — quick product feasibility and proposed customer response:

Summary of what we can commit to in contract:
- Per-tenant "no-training" opt-out: feasible. We'll add a control-plane feature flag that, when set for a tenant, prevents any background replication of runtime traces to long-term training buckets. Implementation estimate: 2 sprints for control-plane + 1 infra sprint to add lifecycle enforcement. Can be prioritized for EverReach as part of a small engineering tranche.

- 30-day retention on runtime traces: feasible with per-tenant lifecycle policies. Note: we should be explicit about what "runtime traces" include (we recommend limiting the definition to request/response metadata + timing + anonymized token counts, and exclude full content unless redacted). This reduces risk and implementation complexity.

Commercial ask (Marissa) — if we accept a one-off engineering prioritization and quarterly attestation, we should discuss a short-term commitment (minimum reserved capacity or 12-mo term) to offset prioritization cost.

Proposed next steps to reply to EverReach in one email (I can draft):
1) Confirm we can implement per-tenant opt-out and 30-day retention as described; define exact definitions (what telemetry fields are in scope).
2) Offer compensating controls (audit logs, signed attestations) and a timeline (2-3 months for delivery).
3) Ask if EverReach would accept an Opt-In Addendum for research/training use or require explicit written opt-in per dataset.
4) Request a short call to finalize wording.

I'll draft the response and send by EOD for legal/security review.

- Aditya
Senior Product Manager, Serving Runtime
